Rashi on Eruvin 41a:10:1.english: I did not hear this ruling - That Ulla established earlier that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:10:2.hebrew: את אמרת ניהלן - רב יוסף חלה ושכח תלמודו, והיה אביי תלמידו מזכירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:10:2.english: You told it to us - Rav Yosef fell ill and forgot his learning, and Abaye, his student, would remind him.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:10:3.hebrew: זו דברי ר' מאיר - דאמר לעיל משום ר"ג: מודה היה שאין משלימין, וכן ט' באב שחל להיות ערב שבת. אבל חכמים אומרים: מתענה ומשלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:10:3.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir - That which [Rabbi Meir] said above in the name of Rabban Gamliel: "He conceded that they do not complete [the fast], and similarly the Ninth of Av that occurs on Shabbat eve." But the Sages say: One fasts and completes [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:11:1.hebrew: מאי לאו - חכמים אכולהו קיימי, בין אחנוכה ופורים, בין אערב שבת. ומדאגמר' רב לר' יוסי בלשון חכמים, ש"מ הלכה כרבי יוסי:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:11:1.english: What, is it not - [Does the statement of] the Sages apply to all of them, both to Hanukkah and Purim and to Shabbat eve? And since Rav taught [the opinion of] Rabbi Yose in the phrasing of "the Sages," learn from this that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yose.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:1:1.hebrew: וכן ערב תשעה באב שחל להיות בשבת - אע"פ שאם חל להיות בחול, לא יאכל שני תבשילין, ולא יאכל בשר, ולא ישתה יין — עכשיו שהוא שבת, אוכל כל צרכו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:1:1.english: And so too, the eve of the Ninth of Av that occurs on Shabbat - Even though if it falls on a weekday he may not eat two cooked dishes, and may not eat meat, and may not drink wine — now that it is Shabbat, he eats as much as he requires.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:1:2.hebrew: בשעתו - שהיתה שעתו עומדת לו במלכותו, דמלך והדיוט הוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:1:2.english: In his time - When his hour favored him during his reign, for he was [both] a king and a commoner.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:2:2.english: To show the halakha - That one does not complete a fast on Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:3:2.hebrew: מבעוד יום - שצריך לאכול מבעוד יום, ומקבל תענית עליו משגמר לאכול, ואע"פ שהוא שבת:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:3:2.english: While it is still day - That he must eat while it is still day, and accepts the fast upon himself once he has finished eating, even though it is Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:3:4.english: And what is the difference to me entering in a state of affliction - For example, where he completed his fast on Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:3:5.english: And what is it to me to leave it while he is fasting - In that he begins his fast while it is still day.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:1.hebrew: ואם התחילו - שהתחילו להתענות כ' או ל' יום, ונכנסו בהן ימי חנוכה או ראש חדש:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:1.english: And if they had begun - That they had begun to fast twenty or thirty days, and the days of Hanukkah or the New Moon occurred during them.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:2.hebrew: שאין משלימין - תענית בחנוכה וראש חדש, להתענות כל היום:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:2.english: That they do not complete - A fast on Hanukkah and Rosh Chodesh, to fast the entire day.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:3.hebrew: וכן בתשעה באב שחל בע"ש - נמי אין משלימין:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:5:3.english: And so too on the Ninth of Av that occurs on Shabbat eve - [In this case] as well, they do not complete [the fast].

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:6:1.english: To annul his statement - And to say that one completes [the fast].

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:6:2.english: I see that the body follows the head - I see, by right and by law, that we must follow the words of the earlier [authorities].

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:6:3.english: And there was no one, etc. - Evidently, one does not complete [the fast].

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:7:1.hebrew: בדורו של רבי יוסי - דהוה בתר הכי, שבקוה לדר"ג וקבעו הלכה כרבי יוסי דמותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:7:1.english: In the generation of Rabbi Yosei - Which was later — they abandoned [the ruling] of Rabban Gamliel and established the halakha in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, that it is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:1.hebrew: מבני סנאב בן בנימין - משפחה היא משבט בנימין, שנפל להן גורל לקרבן עצים בי' באב בימי עזרא, ויו"ט היה להם לעולם, כדתנן בפרק בתרא דתענית:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:1.english: From the descendants of Sena’av ben Binyamin - It is a family from the tribe of Benjamin for whom the lot fell for the wood offering on the tenth of Av in the days of Ezra, and it was a festival for them forever, as we learned in the final chapter of Ta’anit.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:2.hebrew: לאחר השבת - שהוא עשרה באב, והוי יו"ט שלנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:2.english: Until after Shabbat - Which is the tenth of Av, and it was our Festival.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:3.hebrew: טעמא דיו"ט - הא בשאר ט' באב היו משלימין, אע"פ שכל ט' באב הוי ערב יו"ט שלהם. ורבי אלעזר בר צדוק בדורו של רבן גמליאל הוה, כדתניא בביצה (דף כב:), א"ר אלעזר בר' צדוק: פעמים הרבה נכנסתי אחר אבא לבית ר"ג:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:8:3.english: The reason [was that it was] a Festival - Implying that in other [years] on the Ninth of Av they would complete [the fast], even though every Ninth of Av is the eve of their Festival. And Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok was in the generation of Rabban Gamliel, as it was taught in a baraita in Beitza (22b): Rabbi Elazar b'rebi Tzadok said: Many times I entered after my father into the house of Rabban Gamliel.

Rashi on Eruvin 41a:9:1.hebrew: שאני יום טוב דרבנן - כגון האי קרבן עצים — הואיל וקל הוא שמתענין בו לשעות, כדקתני "והתענינו בו", לפיכך משלימין בו ערביות. כלומר, מותר להשלים ערב אותו יום טוב וליכנס לתוכו כשהוא מעונה, דהא אפילו בעיקרו מותר להתענות בו קצת היום. אבל שבת, שאסור להתענות בו קצת לשום תענית — אסור נמי להשלים בו ערביות, שהמשלים ע"ש מתענה במקצת שבת:
Rashi on Eruvin 41a:9:1.english: A rabbinic Festival is different - Such as this wood offering [festival]: Since it is lenient, in that one may fast on it for hours, as [the baraita] taught, "And we fasted on it," therefore one completes [a fast on] its eve. That is to say, it is permitted to complete [a fast on] the eve of that Festival and enter into it while afflicted [from fasting], for even on [the festival] itself it is permitted to fast for part of the day. But Shabbat, on which it is forbidden to fast [even] a bit for any fast, it is also forbidden to complete [a fast on] its eve, for one who completes [a fast on] Shabbat eve fasts during a part of Shabbat.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:2:1.hebrew: [ביצה מגולגלת - בפי' ר"ח: קבלה בידינו כי ר' עקיבא אותה שנה מסוכן היה, והביאו לר"ע הרופאים לגמע ביצה מגולגלת באחרית היום. ור' יהודה לא דקדק; לפיכך סמך על מה שראה, ולא ידע העיקר על מה עשה כך. ותמוז דהאי שתא מלייה מליוה, לפיכך חל תשעה באב בערב שבת, וחסרו אב ובא ר"ה בשבת — תוס' שאנ"ץ]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:2:1.english: ["A slightly cooked egg" - In the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel: We have a tradition that Rabbi Akiva was dangerously ill that year, and the physicians brought [an egg] to Rabbi Akiva for him to swallow a slightly cooked egg at the end of the day. And Rabbi Yehuda did not investigate [the matter]; therefore, he relied on what he saw and did not know the underlying reason why he did so. And they made Tammuz of that year full [thirty days]; therefore, the Ninth of Av occurred on Shabbat eve, and they made Av defective [twenty-nine days], and Rosh Hashanah occurred on Shabbat. — Tosafot of Sens.]

Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:3:1.hebrew: אי אתם מודים בתשעה באב - וא"ת: והא אמר שמואל בפרק מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נד:): "תשעה באב, בין השמשות שלו מותר"? וי"ל: דמ"מ מתחיל מבעוד יום, לפי שאי אפשר לכוין תחילת הלילה. ועוד, דר' יוסי סבירא ליה: בין השמשות כהרף עין, ואין אדם יכול לעמוד עליו. ואין לפרש דהכי קאמר: דהיכא דהפסיק סעודתו, דהוי כמו קבלת תענית בשבת — דהא לא מצי קביל תענית בשבת עליה. ועוד, דאמרינן דאפילו יוה"כ, דתוספת שלו דאורייתא, שרי לאכול אע"פ שכבר הפסיק, כדאמרינן באיכה רבתי: ר' יהודה בן בתירא אזל לנציבין בערבא צומא רבא. אזל ריש כנישתא לזמוני ליה. א"ל: "כבר אכלי ופסקי". א"ל: "אשגחאי עלי, דלא לימא: גברא רבא הוא דלא אשגח עילויה". אזיל עמיה; ומסיק התם דאכל מכל עיגול חד פתיתא, ומכל מאכל פת אחד, ומכל חבית חד כוס:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:3:1.english: "Don't you agree with me with regard to the Ninth of Av" - And if you say: But didn't Shmuel say in the chapter [entitled] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 54b): "With regard to the Ninth of Av, its twilight is permitted"? And one can say: That nonetheless, he begins [fasting] while it is still day, because it is impossible to determine precisely the onset of the night. And furthermore, Rabbi Yosei maintains [that] twilight is like the blink of an eye, and no person can ascertain it. And one should not explain that this is what [Rabbi Yosei] is saying: that where one finished his meal, it is considered like accepting a fast on Shabbat — for one cannot accept a fast upon himself on Shabbat! And furthermore, we say that even [with regard to] Yom Kippur, where adding to it [from the non-sacred to the sacred] is from the Torah, it is permitted to eat even though one has already finished [his meal], as we say in Eikhah Rabbati: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira went to Netzivin on the eve of the Great Fast. The head of the synagogue went to invite him. He said to him: "I have already eaten and finished." He said to him: "Pay heed to me, so that they should not say: He is a great man [and] they did not attend to him." He went with him; and [the Midrash] concludes there that he ate one morsel from each round [of pressed figs], and one piece of bread from each dish, and one cup [of wine] from each barrel.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:5:1.hebrew: מודה היה שאין משלימין - משמע דרבנן דפליגי עליה סברי דאפילו מפסיקין. ולקמן אמרינן: "זו דברי ר' מאיר שאמר משום ר"ג, אבל חכמים אומרים: מתענה ומשלים", אלמא אדרבה — דלרבנן משלימין! ושמא הנהו חכמים דפליגי אדרבי מאיר סברי דמשלימין, והכא קאמר: מודה לרבנן דפליגי ארבן גמליאל, והנהו סבירא להו דמפסיקין:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:5:1.english: "He conceded that they do not complete" - This implies that the Rabbis who disagree with him hold that they even interrupt [the fast]. Yet later we say: "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir, who stated it in the name of Rabban Gamliel, but the Sages say: One fasts and completes [the fast]" — which shows, on the contrary, that according to the Rabbis they complete [the fast]! And perhaps those Sages who disagree with Rabbi Meir hold that they complete [the fast]; but here, it means [that Rabban Gamliel] conceded to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabban Gamliel, and those [Rabbis] hold that they interrupt [the fast].

Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:8:1.hebrew: מבני סנאב בן בנימין - סנאה גרסינן, ולא גרסינן סנאב, דהכי כתיב בעזרא. ועל שם שבטו נקרא "בן בנימין", דגבי עצי מערכה חשיב ליה בפרק ד' דתענית (דף כו.); וכל הנהו דחשיב התם — "בני ארח בן יהודה", "בני דוד בן יהודה" — כולם על שם שבטן. ואע"ג דר' אלעזר בן צדוק כהן היה, כדמוכח בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לו.) גבי: "רבי אלעזר בר צדוק הוה ליה בוכרא" וכו' — שמא אמו היתה מבנימין, או חתנם היה והיה עמהם בסייעתם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:8:1.english: "From the descendants of Sena’av ben Binyamin" - We read "Sena'ah," and we do not read "Sena'av," as so it is written in Ezra. And on account of his tribe he was called "son of Benjamin," for regarding the wood for the arrangement [of the altar, the Mishnah] lists him in chapter 4 of Ta'anit (26a); and all those that it lists there — "the sons of Arah, son of Judah," "the sons of David, son of Judah" — are all [named] on account of their tribe. And even though Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok was a kohen, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 36a) regarding: "Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok had a firstborn animal," etc. — perhaps his mother was from [the tribe of] Benjamin, or he was their son-in-law and was with them in their company.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:9:1.hebrew: שאני ימים טובים מדבריהם מתוך שמתענין בו שעות משלימין בו ערביות - והא דאמרינן בסוף פ"ק דר"ה (דף יט): דימים הכתובים במגילת תענית אסורין בין לפניהם בין לאחריהם; ותנן נמי במסכת תענית בפרק שני (דף טז:): "כל הכתובים במגילת תענית דלא למספד בהון — לפניו אסור, ולאחריו מותר", ועשרה באב כתיב בהנהו דלא למספד בהון — משמע דיו"ט דדבריהם נמי אסור להתענות בו ערביות! הני מילי תענית דרשות, אבל תענית חובה, כגון תשעה באב — מתענין. וא"ת: והיכי פשיט לעיל מרבי יוסי דאיירי בתענית חובה, על בני בי רב דיתבי בתענית, דמשמע דאיירי בתענית הרשות? וכן משמע בשאלתות דמיירי בכל תעניות, ומנהג נמי דאפילו בתענית הרשות משלימין, ובירושלמי נמי אמרינן במסכת תענית בשם רב הונא: "אפילו יחיד הגוזר על עצמו בע"ש תענית — מתענה ומשלים". וי"ל: דשפיר מוכח לעיל, דכיון דאמר ר' יוסי "מתענה ומשלים", אע"ג דתענית ט' באב לא דחי שבת, ש"מ דבמה שנכנס בשבת כשהוא מעונה לא חשיב כמתענה בשבת, וא"כ בתענית הרשות נמי שרי להשלים. אבל ערב יום טוב דדבריהם שייך לפלוגי בין תשעה באב לתענית הרשות: דמה שאסור להתענות בערב יו"ט דדבריהם — לאו משום דחשוב כמתענה ביו"ט, דהא לאחריו נמי אסור, אף על גב דאין מתענין ביו"ט, אלא משום דעשו חיזוק ביו"ט דדבריהם שלא יבא להתענות ביו"ט עצמו; וכי גזרו — בתענית רשות, אבל בתשעה באב לא גזרו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41a:9:1.english: "Rabbinic Festivals are different: since one fasts on it for hours, one completes [a fast on its eve] until evening" — And as for that which we say at the end of the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (19a), that the days written in Megillat Ta'anit are forbidden [to fast on] both before them and after them; and we also learned in a Mishnah in tractate Ta'anit in the second chapter (16b): "[Regarding] all that is written in Megillat Ta'anit [about which it says] not to eulogize on them: [on the day] before it is forbidden [to fast], but [on the day] after it is permitted"; and the tenth of Av is written among those regarding which [it is decreed] not to eulogize on them — which implies that on a rabbinic Festival it is also forbidden to fast on its eve [into the evening]! This applies [only] to an optional fast, but on an obligatory fast, such as the Ninth of Av, one fasts [and completes it]. And if you say: But how did [the Gemara] resolve earlier [the question regarding] the students of the academy who were sitting in a fast — which implies that it was dealing with an optional fast — from [the teaching of] Rabbi Yose, who was dealing with an obligatory fast? And so it implies in the She'iltot, that it is dealing with all fasts; and the custom is also that even on an optional fast one completes [it]; and in the Yerushalmi as well we say in tractate Ta'anit in the name of Rav Huna: "Even an individual who decrees a fast upon himself on the eve of Shabbat fasts and completes [it]!" And one can say: It was indeed properly proven earlier; for since Rabbi Yose said "he fasts and completes [it]", even though the fast of the Ninth of Av does not override Shabbat, conclude from this that by entering Shabbat while afflicted [from fasting], one is not considered as fasting on Shabbat. And if so, on an optional fast it is also permitted to complete [it]. However, [with regard to] the eve of a rabbinic Festival, it is relevant to distinguish between the Ninth of Av and an optional fast: for the fact that it is forbidden to fast on the eve of a rabbinic Festival is not because it is considered as fasting on Yom Tov — as [fasting on the day] after it is also forbidden, even though one does not [thereby] fast on Yom Tov — but rather because they reinforced rabbinic Festivals so that one would not come to fast on the Festival itself. And when they decreed [this prohibition, they did so only] regarding an optional fast, but regarding the Ninth of Av, they did not decree.
